1. Missions and rules

From src/world/missions.js and src/world/mission.js. Score = finish 1000 + stealth 500 (never chased) + 20 per second under par + up to 500 for how well your AI did. Stars: finished · never chased · under par. The alarm countdown starts on the first chase and never resets.

2. Guard AI

Each guard runs a state machine (Patrol → Suspicious → Search → Chase), sees with a 8-unit, 60° vision cone blocked by walls, and chases with A* (Manhattan heuristic), re-planning every 0.3 s. A* returns the same path length as breadth-first search, but expands fewer cells:

3. Mission 1 — drone image classifier (k-nearest neighbours)

The player labels 32×32 CCTV snapshots as guard or civilian; the drone stores them and classifies new people by their 3 nearest neighbours. Measured on 400 unseen snapshots, averaged over 30 random label subsets. With all 30 lab images labelled correctly, the lab's own 10 held-back images score 90 %.

Accuracy by number of labelled images (k = 3).

Accuracy by k, 30 labels. The game uses k = 3: one neighbour can score about the same, but a single mislabelled image then decides every look-alike.

Accuracy when some of the 30 labels are wrong.

The lab warns below 10 labels (overfitting) and when only one class is labelled. A known limitation: with k = 3 the vote-share confidence is overconfident (see challenges).

4. Mission 2 — robot dog (tabular Q-learning)

A 10×10 laser vault. α = 0.2, γ = 0.95, ε from 1 to 0.05, 1,500 episodes, at most 120 steps each. The player sets the three rewards; after training the dog follows the greedy policy. Shortest safe path: 28 steps. Each reward design below was trained on 20 seeds.

Vault extras (added after playtesting: "it always says 28 steps")

The classic vault above stays the reference: with every extra off, training is identical to before (checked: same learned table on 40 seed/reward combinations). Each extra changes what the dog has to learn; 5 seeds each, recommended rewards unless stated.

5. Mission 3 — hacking assistant (two-hop retrieval + language model)

40 fictional emails split into 53 chunks of 2 sentences, embedded as TF-IDF vectors (353 words). The password is spread over three emails (e17, e05, e29), and a retired decoy password sits in another. Hop 1 searches with the question; hop 2 searches with the words of the best hop-1 chunk. The retrieved emails go to a language model (Cloudflare Worker, or the offline fallback).

Trace for "What is the vault password?" (k = 3). Hop-2 query: team executive has rotated audit name mr varma s first robot written capital followed floor number server room

Recall of the 3 clue emails by k (chunk size 2).

Recall by chunk size (k = 3).

Recorded with a local model (Ollama): full recall gave the right password, KESTREL37; with k = 1 (recall 67 %) the model invented ROBOTX37. That is why the debrief scores the assistant on retrieval recall.

  • CSV export: header, one row per event, quoting of commas and JSON details

  • vision: inside the cone is seen; outside the angle or range is not

  • patrol: guard walks its route with A* and loops
  • seeing the player: Suspicious, meter fills, then Chase
  • sneaking fills the meter more slowly
  • losing sight: Search walks to the last-seen spot with A*, looks around, returns to Patrol
  • chase catches a player who stands still; a player out of sight is not caught
  • difficulty tuning: longer range sees further; hard fills faster and moves faster
  • snapshots are deterministic 32×32 RGBA images
  • lab dataset: 30 images to label (balanced), 10 held-back, no overlap
  • README scenario 5: 30 correct labels → test accuracy above 85%
  • README scenario 4: 4 labels → overfitting warning and clearly worse accuracy
  • wrong labels hurt: 40% mislabelled is much worse than correct labels
  • predict: confidence in 0.5..1, empty model answers null, single class warns
  • drone: scans characters in range once, uses the real model output, reports accuracy
  • civilians wander along their route with A*
  • environment: lasers and goal end the episode; walls keep the dog in place
  • README scenario 7: sensible rewards → the dog reaches the drive safely, by the shortest path
  • README scenario 6: a positive reward for touching lasers → the dog learns to hit one
  • no step penalty → the dog dawdles in a loop; too little training is unreliable
  • training is reproducible with a seed; epsilon decays; rewards improve
  • dog: follows the greedy path cell by cell and reports the outcome once
  • Mission 2 map: vault is 10×10 at the dog's origin, blocked for walkers, console reachable
  • classic environment is the original vault: 100 states × 4 actions, shortest route 28
  • random vaults: same seed same vault; always solvable in 22–38 steps; batteries off the shortest route
  • recommended rewards learn the shortest route on random vaults
  • batteries: a small bonus is skipped (28 steps), a bonus worth the detour is collected (38 steps, 2 batteries)
  • puddles: the dog learns a longer dry route and almost always arrives; a dry-floor dog does worse on puddles
  • blinking lasers: on 3 steps, off 3; the shortest route uses the gap (19 steps); a trained dog learns to slip through
  • training challenge: the first run after which the route reaches the drive is recorded
  • views: visits count every step; the learned value is higher next to the drive than at the start
  • mission dog: walks the vault it trained on; on puddles each run is a real roll-out; batteries raise the score
  • map has a drive and an exit on floor cells
  • exit is locked until the drive is picked up
  • a chase starts the alarm once; it does not reset; reaching 0 loses
  • winning with time left on the alarm still counts as a win
  • caught ends the mission and freezes it
  • scoring: three stars for a clean, fast run; fewer otherwise; zero for a loss
  • missions take their own par and alarm times; triggerAlarm starts the alarm once
  • a mission without a drive cell can still be won once the drive is delivered
  • every neon sign hangs over a wall cell, never over walkable floor
  • map parses: size, start and walls
  • collision: centre of a floor cell is free, overlapping a wall is not
  • input vector is normalised so diagonals are not faster
  • walls block movement and the player slides along them
  • a huge frame (tab switch) cannot tunnel through a wall
  • arrow keys and WASD map to the same directions
  • dataset: 40 fictional emails; the password needs three of them; a retired decoy exists
  • text processing: stopwords removed, plurals folded, 'Mr.' does not end a sentence
  • retrieval: the question finds the rotation email first; scores are cosine in 0..1, sorted
  • two-hop retrieval at the default settings finds all three facts; single hop does not
  • parameters matter: k=1 and one-sentence chunks lose facts
  • prompt: contains every retrieved chunk, the answer format and the decoy rule
  • README scenario 8: with the LLM offline the assistant reasons over the retrieved emails
  • assistant uses the LLM answer when the proxy responds; password extraction
  • worker: CORS origin check, input validation, rate limit 20/hour, key stays server-side
  • Mission 3 map: terminal next to a locked door that opens
  • offline reasoning: full recall gives KESTREL37 and names the three clue emails
  • offline reasoning: weak retrieval answers UNKNOWN and says which fact is missing
  • offline reasoning ignores every distractor: robotics-club robot, old floor, other floors, retired password
  • Lab hints agree with retrieval on every setting; the preview answer matches the clues found
  • each ready-made setting shows the behaviour it promises (3 seeds each)
  • after training, the explanation names the real cause and a fix
  • slider hints agree with real training at the measured thresholds
  • mute silences everything: music, sound effects and the alarm siren

9. Screens

10. Limitations

  • Classifier, Q-learning and retrieval figures come from seeded scripts with correct labels or fixed rewards, not from real players.
  • The browser test is quoted from its recorded run; the language-model answer was recorded with a local model, not the deployed Worker.
  • Touch controls are tested in an emulated phone (390 × 844), not yet on many real devices.
  • The public URL is added once the game is deployed (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).

Reproduce

npm test → npm run test:tap (records the unit run) → npm run dashboard (all experiments run inside the build). This file embeds its figures and screenshots and works offline.
